To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the −308 single base polymorphism of TNFA gene is slightly associated to the development of Crohn's disease and, more importantly, to the behaviour of the disease.
the −308 TNF polymorphism is not associated with CD, but it is associated with a more severe form of CD.
the carriage of the TNF2 allele is associated with steroid‐dependent disease, and to a lesser degree with colonic and fistulizing disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a single base pair substitution in the promoter region (−308) of the TNF gene in a large population with well‐defined phenotypes of CD.
the role of genetic factors in determining the clinical behaviour of CD.
the role of TNF gene polymorphisms in the development of CD.

TNF‐α gene polymorphism has a slight but not significant effect on disease phenotype in CD.
the TNF‐α gene polymorphism at position −308 is associated with steroid‐dependent CD.
the −308 TNF polymorphism is not a major genetic risk factor for CD, but it may be a genetic modifier of the clinical course of this disease.
